content.explanation: When JavaScript was created, computers had limited memory, storage, and processing power. Browsers could not afford large runtimes or heavy software stacks. A lightweight language that started quickly and consumed fewer resources was essential. JavaScript fit these requirements and could run efficiently on a wide range of systems.
content.example: A browser running on 8 MB RAM could not easily support heavyweight technologies.
content.analogy: Packing light is important when carrying a small backpack.
content.keyTakeaway: Hardware limits encouraged lightweight browser technology.
